svg.text: Browser-based drone programming platform · Laravel 13 / PHP 8.5 · Inertia v3 + React 19 · three.js + Rapier · Lemon Squeezy subscriptions
The browser flies; the server decides what a flight was worth.
1 · CLIENT — Inertia SPA in the pilot's browser
▪ Wayfinder typed callers — no hand-written URLs
▪ shared props carry plan + granted features (a hint)
▪ sonner toasts on every create / edit / delete
▪ Monaco editor for the pilot’s mission code
▪ three.js scene: city props, obstacles, drone rig
▪ Rapier physics — the airframe is a rigid body
▪ camera rig · flight HUD · console · briefing panel
▪ runs the pilot’s program off the main thread
▪ fetch / XHR / WebSocket / EventSource stubbed out
▪ every drone.* call is a postMessage round trip,
resolved only once physics carries it out
▪ flight path sampled off the frame loop at 20 Hz
▪ grader.ts scores on landing — a preview only,
mirroring the server’s policy so UI is instant
▪ the shutter captures frames during the flight
▪ upload-queue.ts turns a burst into a trickle —
one POST at a time, flight never waits on it
▪ a rejected upload does not stall the ones behind
2 · HTTP EDGE — routing, middleware, asset pipeline
▪ catalog bound by slug, pilot rows by uuid
▪ three.js split into its own chunk
3 · APPLICATION — Laravel 13 · thin controllers, logic in Actions
▪ guards repeated here, never inherited from a page
▪ StoreChallengeAttempt is the trust boundary: it
accepts no score, no stars, no claim of success
▪ Resources shape server state into page props —
answer keys and solution_code never travel
Gates, so can: middleware and React agree
Starter, memoised on the User instance
path against the mission’s own geometry
▪ GradeSimulatorRun is the authority on a score:
the txn, lockForUpdate merge inside it
▪ variant IDs read from config, never database rows
▪ Fortify actions: register, profile, password rules
generation counter, stampede lock, arrays only
route keys, slugs for public catalog content
▪ SQLite in development · MySQL 8 in production
▪ database driver today; Redis in the target
invalidation is one counter bump per attempt
▪ sessions in the database are the one thing
keeping the web tier from being stateless
▪ jobs table exists; app/Jobs is still empty, so
every request does all of its own work inline
▪ never web-readable: each frame reaches the pilot
Inertia visit · attempt POST · photo POST
page props · graded result · expiring URLs
one transaction per attempt · cache bump
▪ Hosted checkout overlay: no card details ever reach this
application, and no price is trusted from the client.
that grants paid access with no session behind it. The
whole `web` group is dropped, and signature checking is
unconditional, so a missing secret fails closed.
▪ 1 · Lemon Squeezy posts a signed event
▪ 4 · the package’s WebhookController writes the subscription
▪ 5 · ResolvePlanForUser reads it on the next request
▪ 6 · Plan gates catalogue depth, Feature gates capability
▪ email verification, password reset, 2FA recovery codes
▪ log driver in development · SMTP in production
▪ Deploy target. .cloud/config.json links this checkout to an
organisation and application, and is git-ignored — it is
machine-local state, not a project artefact.
▪ Production flips CACHE / SESSION / QUEUE to Redis,
FILESYSTEM_DISK to s3, and APP_ENV to production.
an N+1 fails the test suite rather than the live database
Pest 5 — feature tests built on factories
· the client grader must equal GradeSimulatorRun
▪ The suite runs on SQLite + the array cache while
production runs MySQL + a shared store (a known gap).
